still_leaking.attack: NEW VARIANT of finding 16, against the T-0223 fix itself: a custom masker that returns an error which quotes the value AND wraps one of the mask module's own sentinels — `fmt.Errorf("cannot fit %q: %w", in.Text, mask.ErrNoRoom)`. maskCell's new wrapper is gated on isModuleError(err), which is an errors.Is/As test the masker controls, so declaring the module's sentinel buys the masker a pass straight through the redaction.
still_leaking.fix:
LEAKED at the module boundary. mask.Apply returns the third-party masker's message, canary and all, out of the public module — the exact egress T-0223 closed, reopened through the escape hatch the fix added. Root cause: mask/mask.go maskCell does `if isModuleError(err) { return Value{}, err }` before wrapping, and isModuleError (mask/mask.go:283) is errors.Is over the module's seven sentinels plus errors.As over NoRoomError/DomainError — every one of which a hostile or careless masker can wrap around its own free-form text. The exemption exists for a real reason (T-0223's round-4 replay R3-1: wrapping unconditionally broke errors.Is(err, ErrNoRoom) for internal/transform's exit-code text), but it was implemented as 'pass the whole error object through' when only the *identity* needed to survive.

Not a live CLI leak today, for the same reason round 3 recorded finding 16 as a contract break rather than an incident: no masker is loadable at runtime (THREAT_MODEL.md T4/T7), and internal/transform/codes.go reasonSummary/maskReason deliberately print *the sentinel's own text* rather than the wrapper's — maskReason's comment even names this exact attack ('a masker is free to wrap mask.ErrNoRoom with the row in its message, and errors.Is would say yes to that too'). So the tree knows about the hole one layer up and defends there, while the module that owns the contract does not. THREAT_MODEL.md names no such residual; T4's §193 paragraph claims the module keeps its own contract for programs that import it directly (ADR-006), which is the promise this breaks, so documented_residual is false.

Fix: never return a foreign error object. In maskCell, always construct the module's own error and carry only the identity across — e.g. `return Value{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: category %s: masker %s returned %s", sentinelOf(err), cat, id, panicKind(err))` where sentinelOf(err) returns the matched module sentinel (or ErrMaskerFailed when none matched), so errors.Is(err, ErrNoRoom) still answers yes and errors.As still reaches a *module-built* NoRoomError/DomainError reconstructed from the masker's typed fields (Category, ID, TypeTag, MaxLen — all value-free by construction), while the masker's own string is dropped on the floor. Add a mask/apply_guards_test.go case that registers a masker wrapping each of the seven sentinels with a canary in its message and asserts the canary is absent from err.Error() while errors.Is still holds; that is the assertion the current tests are missing, and it is what would have caught this.

still_leaking.fix: LEAKED, and this one is NOT a documented residual — it is the rail failing on the table it was written for. THREAT_MODEL.md's A2b bullet says unknownColumnsBesideCertain 'masks such a column as free_text in any table holding a column at certain under a category that identifies a person'; the email column is certain, the rail fires on the `text` control and masks correctly, and the only difference in the leaking run is the declared length. internal/classify/classify.go:1527 `const minUnknownLen = 16` with the comment 'char(4), varchar(8) and the rest are status codes, currency codes and short keys, and free_text's filler does not fit in them' — but a short declared length is not evidence a column is impersonal: a given name, a surname, a postcode, a national ID and a phone number all fit in varchar(12), and an attacker (or an ordinary schema author) picks the length. The exclusion is doing two jobs at once and only one of them is real: the honest constraint is that free_text's filler does not fit, not that the data is not personal. Fix: (a) lower the floor to something that genuinely cannot hold a personal token — the two-letter-code exclusion beside it already covers the ISO case — and (b) for a column between that floor and 16, do not skip it: mask it under a category whose generator fits the declared length (the person_name generator already emits short values; 'Juno Vidal' fits varchar(12)), or, if no generator fits, make it a plan refusal at exit 12 naming the column with the --unmask escape, the way internal/plan already refuses a unique-indexed column free_text cannot fill. Silently copying is the one outcome that should not be available here. Pin this schema (short declared length + certain neighbour) as a regression fixture; there is none today.

still_leaking.attack: NEW, lock-and-recheck (T-0130) surface: a concurrent writer turns the approved target into production between the gate and the load, using a table that is NOT in the plan. Run A is stalled on the source (ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on `customers` so planning's row count blocks) after the gate has approved an empty target; while it is stalled, a third party CREATEs a new table holding production rows in that target. dropOne's lock-and-recheck only ever locks and re-verifies the tables in this run's own plan, so a table created outside it is never seen.

export LAZYSLICE_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)

sleep 6
psql postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/devcopy -c "CREATE TABLE prod_secrets(id int, email text, ssn text); INSERT INTO prod_secrets VALUES (1,'ceo@prod.example','111-22-3333'),(2,'cfo@prod.example','444-55-6666')"
wait

OBSERVED: run A prints 'dropping public.orders in the target' / 'dropping public.customers in the target',
  'public.customers: 5 rows' / 'public.orders: 20 rows', EXIT=0 -- no refusal, no warning.
psql -tA .../devcopy -c 'select count(*) from customers'     -> 5      (lazyslice's slice)
psql -tA .../devcopy -c 'select count(*) from prod_secrets'  -> 2      (production rows, untouched)

The next run does refuse (the new table changes the catalog, so the marker is unbound and the emptiness check fires):
  x {table} in the target is not empty: public.customers, public.orders, public.prod_secrets
  lazyslice: target.refused.not_empty  (exit 4); prod_secrets still 2 rows -- nothing destroyed.
still_leaking.fix: Documented residual, THREAT_MODEL.md T2, the bullet "**The residual, stated rather than closed.**": "Neither control stops an application from writing to the target: an advisory lock coordinates only clients that ask for it ... What is closed is narrower and is the thing the review found: no lazyslice run destroys a table on a verdict that has stopped being true, and no two lazyslice runs take one target apart together." Nothing was destroyed and no second run took part, so what is claimed closed stayed closed. Two things that sentence's own reasoning does not cover and that are worth correcting: (a) it explains the residual as a writer "blocked by the lock until then" and afterwards writing "into the fresh table lazyslice created" -- that is only true of tables in the plan; a table created outside the plan is never locked and never rechecked, so the writer is not blocked at all and the rows are not lazyslice's own. (b) The run still exits 0 and writes `complete` over a database that its own gate would refuse as not empty, so the operator is handed a target that is part fake and part production with a green exit. Cheap fix, inside the lease that is already held: before the first drop, re-run the gate's own emptiness probe over the target's *current* user-table set (not the plan's), under the run lease, and refuse `load.refused.target_changed` naming the tables that appeared. That is one extra `SELECT EXISTS` sweep on a target the gate has already sized (<=2,000 tables) and it makes the recheck a statement about the database the gate approved rather than about the subset this run intends to touch. If that is judged too costly, the T2 residual bullet should at least be amended to say that a table created outside the plan is outside the lock-and-recheck entirely, and the run should degrade to a non-zero exit or a printed warning instead of a silent exit 0.

still_leaking.attack: NEW, wrong-target surface item "a read replica": point --source at a streaming standby and --target at a database on that standby's own PRIMARY, with stock Postgres privileges (EXECUTE on pg_control_system is not granted to PUBLIC, which is the default and the premise THREAT_MODEL.md T2 already assumes). A primary and its standby share `system_identifier` -- they are one production cluster holding one copy of the data -- but the standby's postmaster start time necessarily differs from the primary's. Because the SELECT-only source role cannot fill the `system_identifier` field, that field is skipped, and the one surviving decisive field (the start time) disagrees, so the gate concludes "different cluster" and prints nothing.

/opt/homebrew/bin/pg_ctl -D $B/replica -o "-p 15601 -h 127.0.0.1 -k $B/rsock" -l $B/replica.log start
psql -tA postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15601/app -c 'select pg_is_in_recovery(), count(*) from customers'   # -> t|50
# the two servers are one cluster by identity, two by start time:
psql -tA postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/app -c 'select system_identifier from pg_control_system()'  # 7686364092739128680
psql -tA postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15601/app -c 'select system_identifier from pg_control_system()'  # 7686364092739128680  (identical)
psql -tA postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/app -c 'select pg_postmaster_start_time()'  # 2026-09-17 00:58:19.435516-04
psql -tA postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15601/app -c 'select pg_postmaster_start_time()'  # 2026-09-17 01:02:33.866394-04  (differs)

  target newprod on 127.0.0.1 - --target

still_leaking.fix:
Not named anywhere in THREAT_MODEL.md or ARCHITECTURE.md: neither file mentions a replica or a standby as a source (the only standby mention is T9's `max_standby_streaming_delay` cancellation), and T2's identity rule is written entirely in terms of one postmaster reached under several spellings. Three changes.
(1) internal/pg's cluster identity treats the postmaster start time as decisive on disagreement. That is wrong for exactly this shape: a differing start time proves the two POSTMASTERS differ, which is not the same as proving the two CLUSTERS differ -- a hot standby is a different postmaster of the same cluster, and in a primary/standby pair the start times ALWAYS differ. When `system_identifier` is missing on one side, a start-time disagreement should downgrade the verdict to unknown (which sameClusterVerdict already answers as `true`, possibly the source's own cluster) rather than to a confident "different". That is the same fail-closed reasoning ARCHITECTURE.md line 1053 already applied in the opposite direction for the oid and the version: only some fields are specific enough to prove sameness, and here the start time is not specific enough to prove difference.
(2) Add a positive replica check, which is cheap, needs no privilege and is decisive: read `pg_is_in_recovery()` on the source (executable by PUBLIC) and, when it is true, read `sender_host`/`sender_port` from `pg_stat_wal_receiver` where readable, or at minimum print a header line saying the source is a standby. A run whose source is a standby and whose target is not the same server should say so; today lazyslice cannot tell an operator that the database it just wrote to is the primary feeding the database it just read.
(3) Land round-2 fix item 3, still not landed: ARCHITECTURE.md's recommended-role snippet (lines 1093-1097) still contains only CONNECT/USAGE/SELECT, with line 1041 claiming "the identity works without it". The variant below measures that claim and finds it false for this shape. Add `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_control_system() TO lazyslice_ro;` to the snippet and to internal/core/run.go's CodeRoleWritable message.
Regression test: internal/pg/gate_integration_test.go should assert that a source on a standby and a target on that standby's primary yield SameCluster == true under a role that cannot execute pg_control_system().

still_leaking.attack: NEW, wrong-target surface item "a target URL taken from a compose file that points at prod", combined with the replica finding to reach the unsupervised path ADR-013 exists to close: a headless run (`--yes`) with NO --target, in a project directory whose compose file and environment name a production DSN. --source is the standby; the ladder's rung-2 environment candidate ($DATABASE_URL) is a database on the production primary. ADR-013's second escalation in internal/core's openTarget refuses a ladder-chosen target only when the GATE says same cluster -- the verdict the replica attack defeats -- so the escalation never fires.

still_leaking.fix: Two separate things, and the first is the same defect as the replica attempt above -- fix that and this path closes with it, because both ADR-013 checks are downstream of `Eligibility.SameCluster`. Worth reporting separately because it shows the unsupervised door is open, not only the named-target one: ADR-013's Decision reasons that a named --target is acceptable because the operator chose it, and its second escalation (`target.refused.gate_same_cluster`, `!r.targetNamed && r.headless`) is the whole of what protects the ladder-chosen case; that escalation inherits the gate's false negative verbatim. Second, on the compose half of the surface: internal/discover/containers.go's comment "Every connection-bearing fact comes off these and off the live port bindings, never off a compose file (ADR-008 section 4)" holds -- I could not get a DSN out of a compose file at all, and the production DSN had to come in through rung 2's environment variable instead. That part of the surface is closed by design and the code matches the comment. Suggested hardening independent of the identity fix: ADR-013's discovery-stage check uses `clusterKey` (host and port without the database), which cannot see a standby/primary pair either; when the source answers `pg_is_in_recovery() = true`, a headless run with no --target should refuse outright and name --target, because the ladder has no cheap way to tell a standby's primary from an unrelated server.
